title: Fragment-density-driven kernel adapter and live compaction pipeline for paged KV
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Paged KV caches suffer from fragmentation and small sparse fragments that increase decode prefill latency and force expensive kernel work on hot decode paths. Existing eviction heuristics treat occupancy and recency but lack a signal for 'fragment density' — the fraction of entries occupied by small non-contiguous fragments — which correlates with p50/p95/p99 decode stalls during mixed-length workloads.

Proposal: Implement a fragment-density-driven kernel adapter plus a lightweight live compaction pipeline that cooperates with the prefill scheduler. Two pieces: (1) Kernel adapter: runtime component that monitors shard fragment-density and swaps to a compact-friendly kernel variant or a hybrid decode path when local fragmentation crosses thresholds. (2) Live compaction pipeline: background, quota-limited compaction tasks that coalesce small adjacent fragments into single page allocations when compaction is predicted to reduce upcoming prefill work. The compactor uses conservative I/O and is admission-controlled by the prefill window to avoid exacerbating tail latency.

Goals and success criteria: Reduce p99 prefill latency by 20-40% in high-mix workloads (short/long sequences), reduce kernel stalls caused by scattery KV lookups, and lower per-token kernel invocation counts for common decode shapes. Maintain <5% additional steady-state CPU/GPU overhead and ensure SLOs are preserved.

Design notes:
- Fragment density metric: sliding-window estimator computed per-shard: fragment_density = (count_fragments_with_size<=X) / (occupied_slots). Default X=64 tokens. Tunable via shard config.
- Kernel selection policy: three-tier: NORMAL -> HYBRID -> COMPACT. Transition hysteresis to avoid flapping; require sustained crossing for 3 prefill windows. HYBRID schedules partial vectorized gather + sequential fallback while COMPACT uses contiguous memory kernels optimized for packed pages.
- Compaction algorithm: opportunistic adjacent-fragment merge with tenant-weighted prioritization, rate-limited to N bytes/sec per shard. Compaction tasks prefer fragments predicted to be prefills by the predictive TTL estimator.
- Prefill scheduler integration: when a prefill request arrives, scheduler consults fragment_density and kernel tier. If HYBRID/COMPACT and hotset predicted, the prefill window may trigger on-demand micro-compaction (local, sub-100ms) for critical spans.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Over-eager compaction can increase write amplification and transient CPU spikes; mitigate by budget, backoff, and tenant weighting.
- Kernel switching increases code-path complexity and test surface. We'll implement feature flags and a runtime trace indicating which kernel path handled each decode.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout 1) unit/integration tests + microbench harness, 2) internal canary on low-traffic tenants, 3) cross-datacenter canary with synthetic mixed-length traces, 4) broad rollout with auto-fallback. Monitoring/alerts defined below.

2025-02-20: Decision: use size threshold X=64 as default after comparing distributions from production traces. Liam to prototype kernel adapter; Asha to spec compactor admission controller.

2025-03-03: Integration test revealed a race between compaction and concurrent eviction; added shard-level compaction token and retry backoff. Adding test cases to cover interleaved compaction + eviction.
2025-03-05: Preparing canary build and canary checklist. Need SRE review for compaction I/O budgets and monitor thresholds.
